title: IMP-0019 shadow rotation advisor: would rotating at semantic boundaries have beaten continuing?
summary: Hypothesis: within-node rotation at semantic boundaries (retry/repair attempt boundaries) would have cost less input tokens than continuing with Orchestrator's re-attempt behavior for a material share of multi-call workers. Method: the deterministic shadow rotation advisor in src/agent_os/orchestrator/rotation_advisor.py, implemented per DEC-0044 (docs/orchestrator-os/self-audit/rotation-advisor.md). The advisor scores each eligible call boundary in past orchestrator runs using a break-even cost model based on IMP-0018's context-economy harness (EVR-0018). For each boundary k, it estimates: C_continue(k) = sum of input tokens for remaining calls (hindsight); C_rotate(k) = estimated fresh-worker bootstrap + structured handoff + targeted retrieval + rediscovery overhead. It recommends rotation only at semantic boundaries where savings > 20% margin. Mode: shadow advice only; no dispatch changes or network calls. Predictions are not yet compared with replayed outcomes. The real-telemetry evaluation requires a host command: `python -m agent_os.cli orchestrate rotation-advisor --out docs/orchestrator-os/self-audit/rotation-advisor-baseline.json`. Synthetic-fixture tests validate the cost model, constants, decision rules, privacy guarantees and shadow-mode invariants.

provenance.source: deterministic shadow advisor over per-call telemetry (no network, no paid compute)
